Preference.app:title: What gets sent
Preference.app:summary:
Sharing is opt-in and off until you switch it on. Only corrections made after you switch it on are sent, about every 6 hours (on Wi-Fi only unless you change that).

One small record per correction: the word as you typed it, the fix we offered (and up to 3 alternatives), what you did with it (kept, undid, picked another, said not a typo, or retyped it as something else), what kind of fix it was, how sure the model was, the model and app version, and the date (no time of day).

Context is at most 2 words before and 1 word after, lowercased. Any word with a digit, @ or :// or longer than 20 letters is dropped on this phone first; if the corrected word itself would be dropped, nothing is sent for it. No app names, no key touches, and no sentences unless you also turn on “Include sentence context”.

With “Include sentence context” on (a separate switch, off by default), each record also carries the rest of the sentence the word was in: up to 24 words before it and 12 after, never past the end of the sentence or the line. Before it is queued, every number, email address, link, @name or #tag, word longer than 20 letters, word mixing letters and digits, and anything that looks like a code or key is replaced on this phone by a placeholder such as <num> or <email>. Names and other ordinary words in the sentence are sent as typed. Switching it off removes the sentences from everything still queued.

Nothing typed in password, incognito, email, web address, number, phone or date fields, or in password managers, authenticator apps and terminals, is ever recorded, so it can never be sent. Sentence context is also never taken from name, address, search-filter or no-suggestion fields. Upload preview below shows exactly what’s queued.

Uploads carry a random ID made by this app, not your name, account or phone ID. The server doesn’t store IP addresses and deletes uploaded records after 90 days. It’s used only to improve this autocorrect.
